sdf_union — 3D sdf_csg op

• Data kinds: sdf × sdf → sdf

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sdf_union(a, b) (to call the implementation directly, import sdf_ops; sdf_ops.sdf_union(a, b); from the registry, ops3d.get("sdf_union"))

Usage

The union of two SDFs, A∪B = the element-wise min(a, b) (inside if either is negative).

The zero isosurface matches the union of both shapes' boundaries exactly. Outside it is an exact SDF (distance to the nearest surface); inside it is a conservative lower bound. a/b only need to be broadcast-compatible.

Computation: np.minimum(np.asarray(a, float64), np.asarray(b, float64)). No other checks -- if the shapes cannot broadcast, numpy raises ValueError; NaN propagates element-wise (np.minimum returns NaN). ±inf propagates exactly (min(a, +inf) = a: interoperates with the "+inf if everything is free" contract of esdf).

Input: 2 SDFs evaluated on the same grid (outputs of sphere_sdf / box_sdf / esdf etc., negative inside, positive outside). The shape may be grid_coords's (nx, ny, nz) or a point list (N,). The distance unit is that of the input.

Returns: float64 of the broadcast shape. The zero crossing (<= 0) is the occupancy of A∪B.

Note: the inside value is a lower bound of "the distance to whichever surface is nearer"; in the overlap region it comes out smaller than the true distance (larger in absolute value). This is a standard property of CSG and does not affect isosurface extraction (marching cubes) or dilation by sdf_offset. To round the seam, use sdf_smooth_union.
